Architecture of the isolated collection and research paths.
Information, fill and label availability under the execution-aligned target.
Audit confusion matrices with class support; row normalization does not create independent observations.
Probability reliability and confidence coverage, including bin support and uncertainty.
Paired audit forecast effects and date-block uncertainty. Lower log loss is better.
Registered controlled contrasts on development outer blocks; intervals preserve date dependence.
Fitting versus outer validation log loss under training-design changes.
Historical instrument/period heterogeneity. Consumed-period slices are descriptive.
Continuous accounts from their original common start; these are not fresh audit allocations.
Recorded exposure, turnover and cost diagnostics under the shared ledger contract.
Registered execution sensitivities; terminal return and path risk answer different questions.
Measured fitting latency by registered variant under differing run order and concurrent host load; these are operational timings, not controlled speedup estimates.
